newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan consumption moderate ahead of tax rise--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan consumption moderate ahead of tax rise--MOF.

text.p: Japan's private consumption has been relatively moderate ahead of a planned rise in the nation's sales tax from April 1, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday.

Asked about reports that the so-called "rush in" buying ahead of the tax rise seems to be weaker than expected, Mitsuzuka said it was true that the buying seemed to be less robust than in the period preceding the introduction of the tax several years ago.
"(Consumption in) houses and cars seems to have settled down. Consumers' attitude seems to be moderate," Mitsuzuka said. "Each household seems to be spending wisely."

Mitsuzuka added that the rise in the consumption tax to five percent from three percent would depress economic growth in the April to June quarter, but he said that as a result of various reforms and deregulation steps the economy would later get back on a recovery path.
The finance minister said the government will announce its steps to boost liquidity in the real estate market on March 31.
The Finance Ministry had previously announced it would draw up measures to help the sagging property market by the end of March but had not set a specific date.

Asked about overnight comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on the U.S. economy, which were interpreted by some as implying a future U.S. credit tightening, Mitsuzuka said he had not heard details yet but added that as a general rule monetary authorities raise interest rates in order to control an overheated economy.
